word_order: SVO — subjects precede verbs which precede objects in the samples (e.g. “Travellers are strongly advised …”).
register: encyclopedic / informational edited prose (Wikipedia-like, formal written text)
target_language_risks: Splitting mid-subordinate clause will break German verb-final ordering and produce wrong word order; pronouns in isolated fragments lose gender/case information needed for correct German nominative/accusative/dative and gendered pronouns; prepositions and particles may need different case or reordering in German so detached prepositional phrases can be mistranslated; idiomatic or phrasal verbs (get along, get in) and compound adjectives may be mistranslated if split.
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer emitting segments at clause-completing punctuation (period, semicolon, colon) or after an explicit clause marker + its clause (e.g., finish the subordinate clause begun by if/when/since/while before emitting). Avoid splitting immediately after commas that are inside numbers or abbreviations (e.g., 6,000; Dr.). Keep subjects with their verbs and retain prepositional/object phrases together when possible to allow correct German case, gender and verb placement.
